latin: Essentia et existentia in quolibet creato realiter distinguuntur.

mentions.context: categories with William Ockham’s distinction between ‘being’, ‘one’ and the categories,153 but this is obviously beyond the scope of this chapter. Thesis 31 brings us to the well-known distinction between essence and existence. It states that essence and existence in any created being are in fact distinguished.154 This distinction is discussed in Thomas’s De ente et essentia.
